label: final copy step of length-3 sequences (outputting orig token 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and never on the original or delimiter steps. Its strongest and most frequent firing is at the last step of length-3 sequences (t=5, outputting the 3rd original token while the input is the 2nd). That step holds about 79% of activation mass, and the top examples are all of the form x y z <DEL> x [y]. The neuron is active on about 69% of those steps. Magnitude depends on the input token: q, l, f, p and 3 give the highest values, while m, y, e, r, s and x often do not fire at all (removing those tokens raises precision to 0.76 but lowers recall). The other ~47% of active steps carry only ~21% of the mass. They are weak activations spread over the last one or two copy steps of longer sequences (to_go=0 holds 89% of mass overall, peaking again at L=9 t=17 and L=6 t=11). It is a low-rate tail, not a clean rule (to_go==0 alone has precision 0.02). It never fires on the first occurrence of a token, i.e. only on copy inputs that repeat an original token.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: l, q, f, p, 3, n; least: k, w, r, y) and the previous input (most: l, 1, z, n, q, p; least: o, x, <DEL>, i); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=3, t=5.
